disease_label_per_paper: Delayed diagnosis of autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2 with adrenal crisis
presentation_summary: 69-year-old woman was admitted with 9 years of progressive fatigue, acutely worsened by high fever, severe anorexia, nausea/vomiting, weakness, and recent 4 kg weight loss over 2 days.

Past history included type 1 diabetes mellitus for 9 years, autoimmune thyroid disease with hypothyroidism for 5 years, thymoma resection 4 years earlier, and 3 years of worsening fatigue and mucocutaneous hyperpigmentation after an unspecified traditional Chinese medicine remedy.
She had a 5-year history of orthostatic hypotension with blood pressure 101/70 to 70/50 to 50/40 mmHg.
On admission she was lethargic and cachectic with dry skin, sunken eyes, cold extremities, and extensive hyperpigmentation of cheeks, nasolabial folds, tongue, palms, soles, elbows, and buttocks.
Admission vitals showed BP 75/47 mmHg, HR 140/min, BMI 21.3 kg/m2, and temperature 39.0 degC.

Labs showed sodium 118.0 mmol/L, chloride 87.1 mmol/L, fasting glucose 20.5 mmol/L, HbA1c 9.2%, urine ketones 2+, pH 7.34, base excess -4.8 mmol/L, WBC 9.8 x10^9/L, CRP 10.59 mg/L, NT-proBNP 22863 pg/mL, hs-troponin T 33.05 ng/L, and creatinine 56 micromol/L.

Immediate IV hydrocortisone 100 mg every 8 hours, saline resuscitation, 10% sodium chloride infusion, insulin therapy, and cardiac support improved BP to 106/63 mmHg within 24 hours. Gastrointestinal symptoms resolved, sodium corrected to 136.8 mmol/L and urine ketones became negative within 72 hours.

non_ranking_workup.source_text_value: Thyroid ultrasound revealed bilateral hyperechoic nodules (C-TIRADS 3) with diffuse parenchymal changes

non_ranking_workup.finding: Complement, eGFR, and urine protein did not suggest nephritic renal failure
non_ranking_workup.source_text_value: Complement components (C3, C4), serum creatinine, eGFR, and urine protein levels were normal
Electrocardiography, pituitary hormone levels, and pituitary CT were unremarkable. Echocardiography indicated normal systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 63%.

confirmatory_findings.conversion_note: Stored as threshold value 1250 with source preserving greater-than sign.

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Cortisol, 60 min after cosyntropin (1 microg) 1.8 microg/dL
Adrenal CT revealed normal morphology without masses or calcification
IAA, GAD antibody ... were positive; Anti-Glutamic Acid Decarboxylase Antibody 102.00 IU/mL
The final diagnoses included AC, APS-2, PAI, AITD (on thyroid replacement), T1DM, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), acute heart failure, severe hyponatremia, and hypochloremia.

actual_treatment: hydrocortisone gradually tapered and transitioned to oral prednisone
fludrocortisone acetate 0.05 mg/day added during follow-up for persistent mild hyponatremia

outcome.clinical_course: Blood pressure improved within 24 hours, gastrointestinal symptoms resolved, sodium and urine ketones normalized within 72 hours, and at discharge electrolytes normalized, hyperpigmentation decreased, and fatigue/anorexia resolved. Later fludrocortisone was added for persistent mild hyponatremia.
outcome.source_text_value: Within 24 hours, her blood pressure improved to 106/63 mmHg, and gastrointestinal symptoms were resolved. Hyponatremia was corrected to 136.8 mmol/L, and urine ketones became negative within 72 hours.

quality_warnings: Cortisol, ACTH, cosyntropin response, antibody profile, adrenal CT, and final diagnoses are confirmatory/context evidence with use_in_ranking:false.

Presentation ranking evidence preserves shock, fever, vomiting/anorexia, severe hyponatremia, dehydration signs, tachycardia, DKA-compatible metabolic stress, hyperpigmentation, and chronic orthostatic hypotension.
